title: Pastoral Shepherding
definition: Pastoral Shepherding is the care, oversight, protection, feeding, and guidance of God's people through faithful spiritual leadership.
summary: Pastoral Shepherding is the caring, feeding, guiding, protecting, and correcting of Christ's flock.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the Good Shepherd and Chief Shepherd of the Church.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Pastoral shepherding is the care, teaching, guarding, and guiding of God's people by appointed leaders. Scripture pictures pastoral work as shepherding souls, not managing a religious platform.

Faithful shepherding includes feeding with the Word, protecting from error, comforting the weak, warning the wandering, and leading by example. It requires tenderness and courage.

Jesus is the Chief Shepherd who lays down His life for the sheep. Pastors must serve under Him and never treat the flock as their possession.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Spiritual leadership can either heal or deeply wound. Pastoral shepherding gives a biblical standard that protects the flock from neglect, performance-driven leadership, and abusive control.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Pray for faithful shepherds and seek care when you need it. Pastors and teachers should measure ministry by faithfulness to Christ and love for people, not platform, control, or applause.
